references.text: Jesus calls Zacchaeus a 'son of Abraham' – the same expression used here about the woman as a 'daughter of Abraham'. Both show that Jesus came to save those who belong to Abraham's family ([ref:Luk 19:9|Luke 19:9]).

The background for Jesus' statement: the woman had been troubled by a spirit of infirmity for eighteen years, which Jesus refers to here by saying that Satan had bound her ([ref:Luk 13:11|Luke 13:11]).

Jesus argues from the lesser to the greater: If one unties an ox or a donkey from its stall on the Sabbath, should not this daughter of Abraham be freed from Satan's bonds? ([ref:Luk 13:15|Luke 13:15]).
Satan strikes Job with painful sores – an example of how Satan binds people with sickness, just as Jesus says here that Satan had bound this woman for eighteen years ([ref:Job 2:7|Job 2:7]).
Peter describes Jesus' ministry as healing all who were oppressed by the devil, which directly connects to Jesus' understanding that this woman was bound by Satan ([ref:Apg 10:38|Acts 10:38]).

A similar Sabbath argument: Jesus asks if they would not pull up a son or an ox that fell into a well on the Sabbath – the same logic as here, that mercy takes precedence on the Sabbath ([ref:Luk 14:5|Luke 14:5]).

Jesus uses a similar argument in Matthew: Which of you would not pull up a sheep that fell into a pit on the Sabbath? A person is then far more valuable than a sheep ([ref:Matt 12:11-12|Matthew 12:11-12]).

Jesus discusses what it means to be Abraham's children – those who do Abraham's deeds are truly his children. Here in Luke, the woman is called a 'daughter of Abraham' who deserves liberation ([ref:Joh 8:39|John 8:39]).

Paul emphasizes that the promise applies to all of Abraham's family – both those who have the law and those who share Abraham's faith. The woman as Abraham's daughter shares in God's promises and deliverance ([ref:Rom 4:16|Romans 4:16]).

Isaiah describes the fast that God has chosen: to loose unjust bonds and set the oppressed free. Jesus' action on the Sabbath fulfills exactly this – to free the woman from Satan's bonds ([ref:Jes 58:6|Isaiah 58:6]).
God's Son was revealed to put an end to the devil's works – Jesus' healing of this woman is a concrete example of breaking Satan's power ([ref:1 Joh 3:8|1 John 3:8]).
